newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt up slightly in late session trading.
newsitem.headline: German debt up slightly in late session trading.

text.p: German debt was trading slightly higher but down from intra-day highs near session-end as traders said the market was becoming infected with a traditional year-end lethargy often seen this time of the year.

By 1610 GMT the March Bund futures contract traded up four basis points at 100.19 having traded between 100.00 and 100.54 today. Meanwhile the April 2006 cash contract was at 102.74, compared with Friday's close of 102.70.
"We are feeling the year-end mood but it is not quite year-end yet," said one trader. Even the latest batch of economic data had little impact, another dealer added.
Even the market's reaction to news the influential November Ifo West German business climate index slipped to 96.9 from a revised 97.3 level in October was limited.

Although some thought the numbers could prompt the Bundesbank into nudging its repo main money market rate, which has been held steady at three percent since late August, slightly lower, the market showed little lasting reaction.

Most dealers predicted the Bund futures contract would spend the next several sessions trading in a range between 100.00 and 100.60 points. "It has become very quiet with foreign pension funds staying on the sidelines," a dealer said.
Even the weekend's stability pact, making the European currency union more likely, failed to spark much interest in trading today.
Chartists said the next support line was seen at 100.07 and after that at 99.92.
